methodology: Replay the baseline and listed successful registration mutations in exported command order. An operation whose before-anchor is at or earlier than a first receipt is applied before that receipt; operations whose bracket straddles it are reported ambiguous. No evaluated first receipt has such an ambiguous bracket.
Registration timestamps are not observed. Adjacent call receipt/terminal values label command-order anchors only, not registration instants, and numeric preference epochs are not mutation timestamps.
The source has no conflicting or reversed registration anchor brackets. All first-recipient records are supported by positive prior rows; absence is asserted only after explicit exported delete rows.

Expiry comparisons use each record expiresAtMs against observed receipt/terminal timestamps. This does not independently verify Redis key TTL, cryptographic validity, client-side grants/receipts, device reachability, APNs delivery, or media connectivity.
Endpoint identity-change flags are reported exactly as exported; their hidden identity fields are not reinterpreted as cryptographic device identity or token rotation.
Mailbox aliases group opaque handles. First observed direction is used as the analysis label, not inferred decrypted invite/call initiation.

Current-source operation semantics were independently verified by the mailbox audit agent using Graphify query 1a0b4914e6e744a4, evidence digest 7a2cfaa5a97cd184; this identifies the emitted endpoint-revoke command signature, not the historical client callback or a token/endpoint joint transaction.

findings.publicationRaceCaveat: Successful monotonic AOF writes cannot reveal a rejected stale publication attempt; this export neither proves nor excludes such a race.
findings.deletionAttribution: Two peer-007 endpoint revocations and adjacent token deletions follow successful mailbox admission. The explicit endpoint-revoke signature is supported by current source, while the triggering app action and historical call outcome causation remain unknown. They cannot explain earlier 090–098 groups; endpoint tombstones do not terminalize call mailboxes.
findings.missingClientAuthorityCaveat: Relay wake rows do not prove that the sender stored the correct received wake grant or that its local issuance/distribution receipt gate was satisfied.

deletionEpisodes.interpretation: The endpoint DEL, device-route DEL and three separate endpoint-tombstone HSET rows match current RevokeEndpoint, so ordinary Redis expiry alone cannot explain this sequence. Endpoint revocation is atomic within its own WATCH/TxPipelined transaction; the adjacent token deletion is separate. The initiating app callback, whether both came from one higher-level lifecycle operation, and their effect on the observed call are not established.

interleaving.caveat: Overlapping envelope spans are not proof of overlapping active media calls.

endpointRevoke.signature: Endpoint DEL, device-route DEL, three separate endpoint-tombstone HSETs, then expiry, in one WATCH/TxPipelined transaction.

endpointRegister.distinction: Endpoint and route records plus one combined high-water HSET, unlike the observed split revoke HSETs.

sourceSemanticsVerification.tokenDeletion: Separate method/key outside the endpoint revoke transaction; adjacent sanitized rows do not prove a joint atomic operation.
sourceSemanticsVerification.scopeLimit: Current source signature match does not establish historical calling lifecycle callback, device action, or per-call media consequence. Endpoint tombstones do not terminalize call mailboxes.
